1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson warrants segregation, a new local pack is a
48	self-contained directory drop.
49	
50	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
51	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
52	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
53	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
54	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
55	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
56	
57	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
58	
59	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
60	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
61	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
62	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
63

=====.claudinite/local/packs/repo-mechanics/RULES.md=====
# repo-mechanics — rules

## A step only the owner can perform goes in its own issue, never in the PR body

A merged PR's body is not a to-do list anyone returns to. PR #12 shipped the
Pages deploy with its one-time setup — *"in the repo's Settings → Pages, set the
source to GitHub Actions"* — as a Notes bullet in the PR description. It merged,
the note went with it, and two days later issue #40 had to re-file that exact
setting, still unticked, alongside the rest of the pipeline's manual settings.
PR #2 did the same with two adoption leftovers in a review comment.

So: when a change lands something that cannot work until a human flips a
repository setting (Pages source, workflow permissions, a repo variable, a
deployment-environment rule), open an **issue** for it — a checkbox per setting,
each saying what breaks while it is off, and a stated closing condition — and
link it from the PR. Keep the note in the PR too if you like, but the issue is
the thing that survives the merge. The exception is a step whose home is an
artifact the owner is already editing (the executor routine carries its own
leftovers in its prompt, per bootstrap); anywhere else, an issue.

And before handing a step over at all, check you actually can't do it — see the
`session-tooling` rule on searching a tool's literal name.

## Check the canon packs before hand-authoring release or CI plumbing

PR #31 hand-rolled this repo's release: `scripts/bump-version.mjs` plus a
version-bump-and-push step in `deploy-pages.yml`, adopting the scheme by copying
what a sibling fleet repo already ran. Within a day, issue #38 and PR #39
deleted all of it — script, bump step, workflow, and the separate `checks.yml` —
for the vendored `static-website` pack, which owns the same pipeline as a
standard with its own checks over it.

The tell was there when it was written: **a mechanic being copied from another
repo in the fleet is a canon candidate, not a file to author here.** The second
copy is the moment to raise it centrally, because a bespoke third copy gets
thrown away and takes its reviewed workflow, its version scheme and its CI entry
with it. So before writing release, deploy, versioning or CI wiring in this
repo, look for the pack that owns it; if none does and a sibling repo already
solved it, that's the finding to report, not the code to duplicate.
=====.claudinite/local/packs/session-tooling/RULES.md=====
# session-tooling — rules

## Never use WebFetch to obtain content you must have

`WebFetch` fails two different ways in this environment, and both were paid for in
one session:

- **It summarizes.** Asked for "the complete verbatim content" of a raw
  `githubusercontent.com` file, it returned a prose description of the document
  instead. The file had to be re-fetched with `curl -sSL -o <scratch>/f.md <url>`
  and read from disk — the correct move the first time.
- **It 403s.** Four consecutive fetches of ordinary publisher pages
  (`gartner.com`, `fortunebusinessinsights.com`, `marketdataforecast.com`,
  `squarerootseo.com`) all returned `403 Forbidden`, so a research pass ended up
  attributing figures to search snippets instead of verifying them at source.

So: when the content itself matters, `curl` it into the scratchpad and `Read` it.
When a page 403s, do **not** retry it or try a sibling URL — take the `WebSearch`
snippet, attribute it to the publisher rather than asserting it, and flag it for
re-verification. `WebSearch` itself works fine and is the right first reach.

**`codeload.github.com` is blocked here too** — `curl … | tar -xz` of a repo
tarball returns 403. Use `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`,
which works through the proxy and yields the same tree.

## A ToolSearch that finds nothing does not mean the tool is absent

Deferred tools are matched by keyword, and the keywords are not the tool's own
vocabulary. A session searched `"create trigger routine scheduled task
automation"`, got back `TaskCreate`/`CronCreate`/etc., concluded there was no
trigger API in the session, and told the owner to create a scheduled routine by
hand — while `create_trigger` was in its tool list the whole time. The owner's
reply was "Why didn't you create the routine? You should have."

Before telling the owner a step is theirs because the capability is missing:
search the **literal name** (`select:create_trigger`), and try the tool. A
negative keyword search is evidence about the query, not about the environment —
and handing the owner work the session could have done is the expensive half of
the mistake.

**`select:` wants the fully-qualified name — for an MCP tool that means the
`mcp__<server>__` prefix.** `select:issue_read`, `select:pull_request_read` and
`select:enable_pr_auto_merge` each return `No matching deferred tools found`,
which reads exactly like an absent tool; `select:mcp__github__issue_read` returns
it. Three executor sessions on 2026-08-01 hit this six times between them (two in
session `1fc538f6`, three in `ecc58551`, one in `000d1bf8`), every one recovered
by a second `ToolSearch` — ~2–4s and a wasted call each, and the usual recovery
(fall back to a keyword query) pulls back five to ten schemas where the `select:`
would have pulled one. Copy the prefix off the deferred-tools list rather than
typing the short name from memory.

## `Edit` needs the `Read` tool — `cat`/`grep`/`sed` do not count

Inspecting a file through Bash does **not** register it as read. A session that had
just explored a freshly-cloned repo with `cat`, `grep -n` and `tail` went straight to
`Edit` on three of those files and got
`<tool_use_error>File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.</tool_use_error>`
three times in a row (23:25:07, 23:25:09, 23:25:15) before backing off to `Read` and
retrying — ~17s and four wasted calls for zero information gained, since the file
contents were already on screen from the shell.

The trap is specific to **exploring with the shell and then editing**, which is the
natural rhythm when surveying an unfamiliar tree (a second repo cloned into the
session, a vendored directory). So: the moment shell output tells you a file is the
one you're going to change, `Read` that exact path before the first `Edit`. Reading a
targeted `offset`/`limit` window is enough — the precondition is the tool call, not
the byte count.

## `enable_pr_auto_merge` cannot be armed in this repo — don't retry it

`main` carries **no branch-protection rule**, and GitHub only offers auto-merge on a
protected branch. Every task that says "open the PR and arm auto-merge" will fail here
until an owner adds one.

Worse, the *first* refusal lies about why. One run got
`The pull request is in unstable status (required checks are failing)` at 05:11:52 while
the `Claudinite world sweep` check was merely still **queued** — it went green moments
later. The agent believed the message, re-checked, retried at 05:12:19, and only then got
the real error: `Protected branch rules not configured for this branch`. ~50s of retries,
a tracker comment that had to be corrected by a second comment, and an otherwise
completely successful run converged as `needs-human`.

So: **do not treat "required checks are failing" from `enable_pr_auto_merge` as a check
failure** — read `pull_request_read` `get_check_runs` and look at `status`, not
`conclusion`. And do not retry the arm: one refusal mentioning branch protection is
final. When the task's own spec authorizes landing without human review (the growth
tasks do), poll `get_check_runs` until the required check *completes* successfully and
then `merge_pull_request` with `squash`. Escalate `needs-human` only when the task
requires a reviewer.

## A scheduled executor turn still needs a `Comment class:` line

The `comment-classification` check treats the scheduler's launch prompt
(`Execute the Claudinite executor: …`) as the owner's latest comment, so **every**
unattended executor session is one blocking Stop-hook finding away from ending. It fired
in all three executor sessions captured on 2026-07-31, without exception.

Knowing this costs 7–11 seconds (emit the line, stop again). *Not* knowing it cost one
session over two minutes of reading `comment-classification.mjs`, `helpers/work.mjs` and
`helpers/repo-context.mjs` to work out why an automated dispatch was being judged as
conversation.

So: when the session's opening prompt is a scheduler dispatch, put
`Comment class: other` in your **first** substantive reply — a command phrase is `other`
by the rule's own wording. Don't wait for the Stop hook to tell you.

## The mounted `.claudinite/shared/` is code without its docs — and its runners are silent when clean

Two ways the engine mount misleads a session that goes reading it, both paid for
on 2026-08-01:

- **The `DESIGN.md` it cites is not vendored here.** Engine source refers to it
  constantly (`// World-scope conformance runner (see DESIGN.md)`,

A session needed the founder's career history for the site's who-we-are section.

wrong, and the page had already shipped in a PR. Stripping them cost a second commit

paragraph — it is a public claim about a named person that they never made. The person
is in the conversation; one question is cheaper than any research. (The site-specific

{"number":103,"title":"product-wiki growth 2026-08-09: re-verification found two misstated citations","body":"Weekly wiki-growth pass (web mode — WebSearch available; WebFetch is blocked at this environment's network egress proxy for every publisher domain involved, which is itself a correction to what the pages previously recorded).

## Questions researched

Both touched pages had the same standing top open question, so this pass spot-checked citations rather than opening new ground:

1. **audience/** — *"Re-verify the Gartner and trust-signal figures at source."*
2. **consulting-market/** — *"Re-verify the market-size, CAGR, segment-growth and pricing figures at source."*

Both re-verifications came back as **corrections, not confirmations**. Neither page had a figure that survived unchanged.

## What changed, and where

### `product-wiki/audience/README.md`

- **Correction:** the 67% rep-free figure carries a qualifier the first pass dropped — Gartner's headline is 67% prefer a rep-free experience **"for at least part of their purchase."** The page stated it flatly. Correction recorded in the body with its why; the header bullet rewritten to carry the qualifier.
- **Correction:** the 2026 release's sample (n=646, fielded Aug–Sep 2025) is *not* the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample behind the 69% website-vs-seller and 73% outreach figures — that sample belongs to the 2025 release. Both are now stated explicitly so they can't be read as interchangeable.
- **New section, "The validation paradox, and the AI reader."** A *later* Gartner release the page had not seen (2026-05-20, n=645) inverts its top-line reading: in the same buyer population, **70% prefer a completely digital self-service experience** *and* **69% prefer to validate AI-generated insights with a sales rep.** So rep-free buying is not the unambiguous good news the first pass recorded for a firm with no sales team — buyers self-serve the research and then want a human to confirm it. That validation moment currently has no owner on this site, which is a requirement, not a nice-to-have. (Explicitly disambiguated in the body from the *other* 69% already on the page — two unrelated Gartner findings landing on the same number.)
- **New finding:** buyers used an **average of seven information sources**, and **45% used GenAI, primarily to gather vendor and product information**. For a large minority of visits the site's first reader is a model summarising it for the buyer — so claims carried by layout rather than by text degrade through that channel. Partly answers the standing "what do they search for on the way" question: increasingly they don't search, they ask.
- Header: flat 67% bullet rewritten; two bullets added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected: the cause is this environment's **egress proxy**, not publisher 403s as first recorded — `gartner.com`, `digitalcommerce360.com`, `demandgenreport.com` and `businesswire.com` are all unreachable here, so no primary *or* secondary carriage is directly readable and re-verification at source needs a human.

### `product-wiki/consulting-market/README.md`

- **Superseded (not deleted, with its why):** the "$14.1bn in 2026 → $116.81bn by 2035 at ~26.5% CAGR" headline was **misattributed**. Fortune Business Insights' current report says **$11.91bn in 2026 → $73.89bn by 2034 at 25.6%**. The $14.08bn / 26.49% pairing the first pass rounded belongs to **Business Research Insights**, a different firm. The **$116.81bn-by-2035 endpoint could not be reproduced from any source found** and is marked unverified rather than removed.
- **The larger finding, now a table in the body:** four firms' 2026 estimates for the same named market span **$11.91bn to $38.7bn (3.3x)** with CAGRs from **18.4% to 35.8%**. That's a disagreement about what "AI consulting services" includes, not measurement noise. The page now states that **no unattributed headline market-size number is quotable** — a more useful answer to "re-verify at source" than a confirmation would have been.
- **Re-confirmed:** SMB AI consulting growing ~25.7% annually, outpacing enterprise. Unaffected by the spread, and the positioning argument built on it still stands.
- **New, against the standing geography question:** North America is **38.13% of the 2025 market**. So the US-centricity of every source this wiki has found is not evidence the market is American — the majority of the category sits outside the sources' focus.
- Header: market-size bullet rewritten to the spread; geography bullet added (7 total, at the cap).
- Citation caveat corrected (same egress-proxy cause), and the pricing benchmarks explicitly flagged as **not** re-checked this pass.

`product-wiki/brand/README.md` was read end to end and **deliberately left untouched** — this pass surfaced nothing citable for it, and padding it would be worse than leaving it.

## Citations added

audience/:
- ``https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-20-gartner-survey-finds-sixty-nine-percent-of-b-two-b-buyers-turn-to-sales-reps-to-validate-ai-generated-insights`` — the validation finding, 70% fully-digital, 45% GenAI, seven-sources average, n=645 / Aug–Sep 2025
- https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2026/03/17/gartner-b2b-buyers-rep-free-purchasing-ai-reshapes-sales/ — n=646 / Aug–Sep 2025 and the "at least part of their purchase" qualifier
- https://www.demandgenreport.com/industry-news/news-brief/gartner-67-of-b2b-buyers-prefer-a-rep-free-experience/52142/ — second independent report of the same release
- ``https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260520585188/en/Gartner-Survey-Finds-69-of-B2B-Buyers-Turn-to-Sales-Reps-to-Validate-AI-Generated-Insights`` — wire carriage of the May release
- (existing 2025 Gartner release annotated as the origin of the n=632 / Aug–Sep 2024 sample)

consulting-market/:
- https://www.businessresearchinsights.com/market-reports/ai-consulting-services-market-119843 — $14.08bn / 26.49%, the actual origin of the first pass's headline
- https://markwideresearch.com/ai-consulting-services-market — $38.7bn 2026 → $176.96bn 2035 at 18.40%
- (Fortune Business Insights and Market Data Forecast entries re-annotated with their current, corrected figures)

**Every figure above is attributed from search-result summaries, corroborated across independent searches — not read at source, because this environment cannot fetch any of these domains.** That is recorded on both pages rather than glossed, and it is why this lands as an unmerged PR for review.

## Open questions left for the next run

Added by this pass:
- With 45% of buyers researching via GenAI, is this site legible to a model reading it on a buyer's behalf, and what specifically would make it more so?
- Who supplies the human validation moment 69% of buyers want, when there is no sales team — is a named founder with a real reply address enough, or does it take a bookable call?
- If the site cites a market size at all, whose definition of "AI consulting services" does it adopt?
- Where does the unverified "$116.81bn by 2035" figure come from? Nothing found this pass reproduces it.
- Re-verify the pricing benchmarks ($5k–$25k per project, $150–$350/hr) — untouched since the first pass, and now the only figures on that page with a single unchecked origin.

Sharpened rather than removed:
- Re-verification at source is **not achievable by any agent pass here** while the egress proxy blocks the publishers; it needs a human or an unblocked environment.
- Geography: North America is only 38% of the market — where does Missing Bulb actually sell?

Untouched and still open: the regulated-category question, the referral-path question, the first-screen question, the substitute-proof question, and consulting-market's wedge, published-pricing, category-definition and direct-small-competitor questions.

No requirement was moved — `product-wiki/product-requirements/` is untouched, per the isolation rule. The validation-moment finding is the one most likely to want a requirement change, and it waits for a human here.

.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/RULES.md:48:- Keep a single source of truth for derived or duplicated data — generate the rest from it instead of hand-editing, and have a test fail if it drifts. Split a fact across more than one place only when a technological constraint forbids a single home, and then have the drift-guard test state, in its own text, the two-or-more places it watches and why the split is forced — so an invisible coupling becomes a self-documenting, reviewed one, and the next reader knows the duplication is deliberate and where its other half lives. When the duplicate mirrors executable logic you can't generate from (e.g. a static list shadowing a set of predicate/matcher functions), drift-guard it by *executing the real logic* against the list in both directions — every entry accepted by some predicate, and every predicate satisfied by some entry — rather than parsing the logic out. When a value must be copied into files that can't share an import (a label spanning a YAML workflow guard and a JS module; a repo slug in prod code and its test), declare it as a `sharedConstants` entry in `.claudinite-checks.json` — its `value`, the expected per-file `counts`, and a `what` naming the places and why. Declared counts are matched against the *flat* literal (comments included), so keep a guarded value on one line wherever it appears — an occurrence wrapped across a line break is invisible to a `grep`/`sed` rename alike. For a value that must stay in sync but *changes over time* (a version string bumped each release), set `regex: true` and give a pattern instead of a literal — every match must then be identical across the declared files, so the guard never needs re-pinning on a bump.
.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/RULES.md:49:- Honor separation of concerns in what you write — code comments and Markdown instructions alike: when file A uses or references file B (a module A imports, or a doc/procedure set A points to), A may state *what* it needs from B or *that* it delegates to B, but never restate *how* B does its job or re-spell the procedures B owns. B's mechanism lives in one place — with B. Copying it into A leaks B's internals across the boundary and springs the same drift trap as any duplicated source of truth: change B and A's paraphrase silently goes stale, with nothing to catch it. Point to B instead of paraphrasing it.

1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11	
12	Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:
13	
14	- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
15	  applies to you.
16	- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
17	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
18	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
19	
20	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
21	
22	`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
23	
24	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
25	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
26	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
27	  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
28	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
29	  materializing it is baselining's converge job, not yours.
30	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
31	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
32	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.
33	
34	## 2. Arm auto-merge
35	
36	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
37	it once this repo's required checks pass.
38	
39	## 3. When the arm is rejected
40	
41	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
42	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
43	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
44	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
45	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
46	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
47	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
48	  PR's **head sha**:
49	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
50	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
51	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
52	    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
53	  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
54	    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
55	    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
56	    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
57	    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
58	    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
59	    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
60	    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
61	    unseen check does not survive anything.
62	
63	## Never
64	
65	Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
66	arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
67	manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
68	are always legal outcomes.

1	# session-tooling — rules
2	
3	## Never use WebFetch to obtain content you must have
4	
5	`WebFetch` fails two different ways in this environment, and both were paid for in
6	one session:
7	
8	- **It summarizes.** Asked for "the complete verbatim content" of a raw
9	  `githubusercontent.com` file, it returned a prose description of the document
10	  instead. The file had to be re-fetched with `curl -sSL -o <scratch>/f.md <url>`
11	  and read from disk — the correct move the first time.
12	- **It 403s.** Four consecutive fetches of ordinary publisher pages
13	  (`gartner.com`, `fortunebusinessinsights.com`, `marketdataforecast.com`,
14	  `squarerootseo.com`) all returned `403 Forbidden`, so a research pass ended up
15	  attributing figures to search snippets instead of verifying them at source.
16	
17	So: when the content itself matters, `curl` it into the scratchpad and `Read` it.
18	When a page 403s, do **not** retry it or try a sibling URL — take the `WebSearch`
19	snippet, attribute it to the publisher rather than asserting it, and flag it for
20	re-verification. `WebSearch` itself works fine and is the right first reach.
21	
22	**`codeload.github.com` is blocked here too** — `curl … | tar -xz` of a repo
23	tarball returns 403. Use `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`,
24	which works through the proxy and yields the same tree.
25	
26	## A ToolSearch that finds nothing does not mean the tool is absent
27	
28	Deferred tools are matched by keyword, and the keywords are not the tool's own
29	vocabulary. A session searched `"create trigger routine scheduled task
30	automation"`, got back `TaskCreate`/`CronCreate`/etc., concluded there was no

- **It is blocked at the network egress proxy — which is not the same as a
  publisher 403, and this rule said 403 for a week.** The fetcher's actual reply is
  `{"error_type":"EGRESS_BLOCKED","domain":"www.gartner.com","message":"Access to
  www.gartner.com is blocked by the network egress proxy."}`. One 2026-08-09 research
  pass collected nine of them: `gartner.com`, `fortunebusinessinsights.com`,
  `marketdataforecast.com`, `digitalcommerce360.com`, `demandgenreport.com`,
  `businesswire.com`, `barchart.com`, `debriefing.io`, `techintelpro.com`.

So: when the content itself matters, `curl` it into the scratchpad and `Read` it.
`WebSearch` itself works fine and is the right first reach.

The corrected cause changes what to do after a block, in two ways. A publisher 403
is per-site, so a wire service or an independent report carrying the same release is
a live alternative to try; an egress block is not — in that one session it took out
the primary release **and** every secondary carrier of it. Don't work down a list of
alternative URLs hoping one is reachable. And don't file "re-verify at source next
pass" as an open question: no agent pass here can ever close it. Write it as needing
a human or an unblocked environment, so it stops being re-attempted.

**A snippet gives you the number, not its publisher.** Working from search summaries,
the first wiki pass attributed "$14.1bn in 2026 / ~26.5% CAGR" to Fortune Business
Insights. Those are Business Research Insights' figures ($14.08bn / 26.49%); Fortune
publishes $11.91bn / 25.6%. Corroborating a figure across several snippets does not
corroborate **who published it** — the snippets quote each other. When you cannot open
the report, attribute a number to the firm a source explicitly names as its origin,
and when sources disagree about that, say so rather than picking one.

## `ScheduleWakeup` wants a `prompt`, and its refusal is not "this tool isn't for you"

Every executor session here hands the real work to a subagent and then wants a fallback
heartbeat in case the completion notification never lands. Five captured sessions tried
it. Three passed only `delaySeconds` and `reason` and got back

> `` `prompt` is required when `stop` is not true ``

(2026-08-08 on issues #86 and #89, 2026-08-09 on #105). The two that also passed a
`prompt` were armed normally — `Next wakeup scheduled for 03:26:00 (in 1524s)` — so the
tool works here and is the right reach.

The ~2s rejection is not the cost. What it cost is the conclusion: two of the three
sessions decided out loud that the tool "is for `/loop` mode, not applicable here" and
moved on, and #105 spent a further call on `ScheduleWakeup {stop: true}` cancelling a
wakeup that had never been set. All three then sat waiting on a bare task-notification
with **no fallback armed while believing they had one** — precisely the safety net an
unattended run has no way to notice is missing.

So: on any `ScheduleWakeup` that isn't `{stop: true}`, pass `prompt` — what the woken
turn should resume doing. And read that message literally: it names an argument you
left out, not a mode you are not in.

## Key an escalation issue to the root cause, not to the cycle that hit it

A maintenance cycle that meets a blocking finding it must not guess at escalates by
opening an issue. When the cause is upstream and unfixed, *every* later cycle meets the
same finding — so the decision that matters is what the **second** filing does.

`check_the_world`'s blocking `declares unknown pack "claude-code-web-users-support"` has
now recurred on PRs #85, #88, #90, #104 and #106. The first run opened #87 and the next
correctly logged its recurrence as a comment there. The 2026-08-09 run opened **#92**
instead, its stated reason being that PR #90 "is a different cycle/branch than the ones
already logged here." True, and irrelevant: one unresolved upstream cause now carries two
open `needs-decision` issues, its recurrence history is split across both, and a
tidy-issues pass had to spend itself cross-linking them (*"see #87 for the running
history"*, *"see #92 for the latest recurrence"*) while being permitted to close neither.

So: before opening an issue for a blocking finding, search the open issues for the
finding's own text and comment on the match instead. A new branch, a new PR number or a
new dispatch issue is not a new finding. One issue per cause is what keeps "has anyone
decided this yet?" answerable — and what stops a standing upstream defect from minting a
fresh issue every day.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: prose-to-checks
3	description: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
4	---
5	
6	# Convert existing prose to checks
7	
8	A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs: prose that is always-testable but was never converted
9	becomes a check, so the packs keep shedding context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is
10	first learned.
11	
12	## Two callers, differing only in scope
13	
14	- **The upgrade pass**, as the last step of a
15	  [growth-extract](../../tasks/growth-extract/task.md) run: the scope is the prose **that run just
16	  wrote**. Extraction already descends the promotion ladder per lesson, but a lesson written as prose
17	  under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides, so it gets asked once more before the
18	  PR opens. Never widen from here into the standing backlog.
19	- **The weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../../tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)**: the scope is the
20	  **standing backlog** — everything under the pack paths configured for this repo, which the task
21	  passes in its Context. A consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by
22	  default — projects don't improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core
23	  `packs/`. Read the prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them).
24	
25	Plus on demand, when someone asks. Either way: never edit a read-only mounted canon pack under
26	`.claudinite/shared/`. Everything below is identical for both callers.
27	
28	## First gate — a working rule, not a product statement
29	
30	Before asking whether a rule is *testable*, ask whether it belongs to a pack at all: **does it govern
31	how we work, or state what the product does?** A pack — canon or local — homes the conventions,
32	gotchas and review discipline that recur across tasks whatever the feature happens to be. A rule
33	asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
34	each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves
35	it (the full rule lives in
36	[generate-project-instructions](../generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md)).
37	
38	This gate comes **first** because product statements sail through the check-the-world test below —
39	"this module must export `X`" has an obvious static signature. Converting one splits a feature's
40	definition across two systems and lands half of it in the one no test of the product ever reads.
41	Load-bearingness is not the test: a real gap in product coverage is a *requirements* gap.
42	
43	A product statement already sitting in pack prose is mis-homed, and a sweep is not the place to
44	re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
45	candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.
46	
47	## What to look for — the check-the-world test
48	
49	For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
50	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
51	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
52	
53	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
54	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
55	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
56	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
57	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
58	
59	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
60	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
61	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
62	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
63	
64	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
65	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
66	
67	## How to convert one
68	
69	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
70	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
71	
72	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
73	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
74	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
75	
76	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
77	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
78	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
79	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
80	   doesn't ship.
81	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
82	   directional by kind.
83	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
84	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
85	
86	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
87	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
88	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
89	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
90	check to the same fixture bar.
91	
92	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
93	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
94	
95	## Coming out: the deletion test
96	
97	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
98	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
99	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
100	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
101	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
102	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
103	
104	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
105	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
106	carries.
107	
108	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
109	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
110	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
111	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
112	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
113	went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
114	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
115	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
116	
117	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
118	**reader**, not mechanized.
119	
120	## Bounds
121	
122	- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
123	  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
124	- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
125	  *landed* check now enforces.
126	- Run the suite and the sweep green before the PR goes up, and never push to `main` directly. The
127	  sweep opens its own PR for the owner's approval; the upgrade pass adds its conversion to the
128	  growth-extract PR already being opened, and opens none of its own.
129
